paper_metadata.title: Effect of Ti/Nb/Ta addition on high-temperature microstructural stability of coherent γ/γ′ in Ni–Al–(Cr,Mo,W) superalloys

Button ingots of each experimental alloy, ~ 30 g in mass, were prepared using high purity Ni (99.9 wt%), Cr (99.9 wt%), Mo (99.5 wt%), W (99.5 wt%), Al (99.9 wt%) Ti (99.9 wt%), Nb (99.5 wt%), and Ta (99.9 wt%) in a vacuum arc-melting unit equipped with water cooled copper hearth and a tungsten electrode. Each ingot was melted six times with flipping after each cycle for homogenous melting throughout the ingot under a partial Ar atmosphere.

All alloy samples were solution-treated at 1573 K for 15 h and subsequently aged at 1173 K for 50, 100, 200, and 500 h, respectively. All alloy samples were water-quenched following solution-treated and aging treatment.
